title: Testing spmatrix vs sparray parity with config_context(sparse_interface=...)
answers: how to test an estimator with sparse arrays instead of sparse matrices
compare results between spmatrix and sparray backends
body:
To check that an estimator behaves the same under both sparse backends, fit it twice inside `sklearn.config_context(sparse_interface="spmatrix")` and `sklearn.config_context(sparse_interface="sparray")` and compare outputs. Internal sparse objects (e.g. kneighbors_graph results) then follow the configured interface, which surfaces sparray-only issues like int64 indices.
Example: sklearn/manifold/tests/test_spectral_embedding.py:test_spectral_embedding_sparse_interface_sparray uses make_blobs(n_samples=30), fixed random_state and eigen_tol, then compares with _assert_equal_with_sign_flipping(..., tol=1e-5) because eigenvectors are only defined up to sign.
A bug fix needs a changelog fragment at doc/whats_new/upcoming_changes/<module>/<PR number>.fix.rst, named with the real PR number.
applies: Writing non-regression tests for estimators that build or consume sparse data internally
